1. The petitioner filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1989, seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the injures sustained by him in the road traffic accident occurred on 16.08.2024.
2.

It is the case of the petitioner that, on 16.08.2024 at about 11.30 a.m., within the jurisdiction of Kaggalipura Police Station, infront of land property of Dayanandasagar, near Kulakamale village bridge, Kaggalipura - Bannerghatta Road, Bangalore South Taluk when the petitioner was riding the M.V.C.No.6829/2024 SCCH - 7 unoffending Suzuki Avenis Scooter bearing reg. No.
KA-05-LM-2259 along with deceased Narayana.H.V., as a pillion rider, at that timer the driver/accused of offending TATA XPresT- Electric Car vehicle bearing reg. KA-03-AK-4515 drove the same from Bannerghatta towards Kaggalipura road in a high speed, rash and negligent manner so as to endangering human life and dashed against the hind portion of the unoffending vehicle, as a result, the Petitioner and pillion rider of the unoffending vehicle fall on the road and the petitioner and pillion rider have sustained grievous injuries and pillion rider/Narayana H.V., was died and the Petitioner has sustained grievous injuries on his left forearm.

Thereafter Petitioner was shifted to CDSIMER Hospital, Harohalli wherein he was treated as inpatient from 16.08.2024 to 26.08.2024 and he has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenditure and other incidental charges.
In this regard the Srinivasa H.V., has lodged complaint before the Kaggalipura police station.

Accordingly,
a case was registered in their Crime No.270/2024 and prepared F.I.R. for the offence punishable under sections 281, 125(b) and 106 of BNS and submitted to the jurisdictional judicial Magistrate and the superior M.V.C.No.6829/2024 SCCH - 7 officers and investigation was taken up by the investigating Officer.

3. Further it is contended that, prior to the alleged accident the Petitioner was hale, healthy and he was aged about 29 years and he was doing hotel business, SS chicken Centre, Kaggalipura and earning sum of Rs.30,000/- p.m.
Due to the injuries sustained in the alleged accident he lost his income and future prospective life, happiness, and earning capacity and become disabled and dependent.
The alleged accident is occurred due to fault and negligence act of the driver of the offending Car bearing Reg. No.KA-03-AK-4515.
Respondent No.1 is the RC.
Owner and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the said offending vehicle, as such the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to Petitioner.

Hence Petitioner filed the present claim petition for Santhosh S vs Lithium Urban Technologies Pvt Ltd on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182244962/
2 seeking compensation.

In the written statement of respondent No.2, Respondent No.2 the Insurance Company has admitting that, the offending Car bearing Reg. No.KA-03-AK-4515 was duly insured with it and the same is valid on the date of the accident and denied the petition averments in part.
Further it has contended that the insured vehicle is not involved in the accident.
The insurer liability is subjected to validity of the DL, permit and other documents as per the law.
Further it is alleged that there is no compliance of provision under Section 134(C), 158(6) of M.V. Act.
Further it is contended that the alleged accident is occurred due to fault of the rider of the unoffending vehicle and no fault of the driver of the offending vehicle.
As such the insurance company is not liable to pay any compensation and in order to get compensation the Petitioner has constrained to file the present claim petition.

Further it is denied that the age, income and occupation of the Petitioner and the petition is false and frivolous in the eye of law and the quantum of compensation claimed by the claimants is exorbitant and reserves the right u/s.170 of M.V. 13. In the cross-examination of PW-1 by the counsel for Respondent No.2, he has deposed that,
when he was riding the unoffending Suzuki Avenis Scooter along with deceased Narayana.H.V., as a pillion rider, at that time the driver of offending car vehicle dashed against the unoffending vehicle,

Further he has denied that he has not possessing valid driving licence and the unoffending vehicle is not duly insured and he was not wearing helmet at the time of accident.
Further he has denied that the alleged M.V.C.No.6829/2024 SCCH - 7 accident occurred due to his negligence and fault and no fault of the driver of the offending vehicle.

Further he has deposed that after the alleged accident he was shifted to Government hospital and thereafter for higher treatment he was shifted to Dayananda Hospital and he was informed regarding the alleged incident to the hospital.
He has not produced the estimation certificate from the doctor regarding the future medical expenditure of Rs.1,00,000/-.
He has not obtained disability certificate from the doctor.
He will produced the details regarding his follow-up treatment.

Further he has deposed that prior to the alleged accident he was doing hotel business and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m., and he has not produced the documents to show such income earning from that business.
Further he has denied that he was not doing that business and not earning such income.
Further he has denied that he has not sustained grievous injuries and he has not undergone surgery.
Now he cannot lift the weight from his hand due to injuries sustained in the alleged accident.
Further he has denied that he is hale and healthy and he is not having any disability.

Further he has denied that in order to get more compensation in collusion with the police he has M.V.C.No.6829/2024 SCCH - 7 falsely implicated the driver of the offending vehicle and registered false case against him and falsely implicated the offending vehicle and he has produced concocted created documents and filed false evidence affidavit and deposing falsely.
During the cross examination Pw.1 has consistently deposed on the lines of the petition/prosecution case and he has made those versions, which could not be shattered in cross examination.

14. The Respondent No.2 contended that the accused is innocent and falsely implicated by the police, but in order to prove its version the Respondent No.2 has neither stepped into the witness box, nor produced documents and any how the Respondent No.2 cross- examined the PW-1.

sentences.text:
The evidence of Pw.1, Ex.P-1/FIR, Ex.P-2/Complaint,
Ex.P3/spot mahazar, Ex.P.4/Spot Sketch, Ex.P.5/MVA Report, Ex.P6/Wound Certificate and Ex.P-7/Charge Sheet clearly establishes that the alleged accident occurred at the spot.
It is not in dispute as to the aspect that, the Petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the alleged incident.
Because, for the above reasons collectively it is clear that, the accident happened due to rash and negligent act of the accused.
It is evident that injuries noted in the Ex.P6/Wound Certificate would be caused by a road accident.
At the same time, it has come out in evidence that the alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.
Matters being so, acts of the accused person clearly constitute the offences punishable under sections 281, 125(b) and 106 of BNS.

Thus because of such negligent act of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle, it resulted in the injuries of M.V.C.No.6829/2024 SCCH - 7 the innocent young man/Petitioner aforesaid, as he/accused drove the said offending vehicle very rashly or negligently on the spot.
Therefore, the alleged accident occurred due to the fault of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle.
Accordingly I answered Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
20. Issue No.2:-

The Learned counsel for the Petitioner has contended that, the injured Petitioner was aged about 29 years and he was doing hotel business at SS Chicken centre, Kaggalipura and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m., and the Petitioner has incurred heavy expenses towards medical expenditure.

As such the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head of pain and suffering, mental agony, medical expenses, special diet, conveyance, loss of future income due to disability, loss of amenities and loss of income during laid up period and prays to award the compensation as prayed in the petition.

21. On the other hand, the learned counsel for Respondent No.2 insurance company contended that even though the Petitioner claimed that his earning was about Rs.30,000/- p.m., the same is not established by the claimant by producing the documents.
Since the Petitioner has not established M.V.C.No.6829/2024 SCCH - 7 his income, he is not entitled for compensation towards such prospects and hence prays dismissal of the petition.

22. The petitioner contended that as on the date of the accident he was aged about 29 years and he relied on the Ex.P.10/Adhar Card of the Petitioner, wherein the date of birth of the Petitioner is shown as 01.01.1995 and this accident was took place on 16.08.2024.
Hence it is clear that as on the date of the accident the Petitioner was aged about 29 years 7 months.
Hence the age of the Petitioner is considered as 29 years.
23. It is not in dispute that the Petitioner sustained injuries in the road traffic accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver/accused.
In the instance case the petitioner claimed that he was doing hotel business at SS Chicken centre, Kaggalipura and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.,
But he has not produced single piece of document to prove his actual income.

In the absence of proof of income the notional income has M.V.C.No.6829/2024 SCCH - 7 to be Santhosh S vs Lithium Urban Technologies Pvt Ltd on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182244962/

As per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority, for the accident taken place in the year 2024, the notional income of the Petitioner is taken at Rs.15,750/-.
24.

In the chief examination of PW-2/Dr.Nagaraj.B.N.,, Orthopedic Surgeon deposed that in the alleged road traffic accident the petitioner has sustained left closed extra articular distal end radius fracture with DRUJ subluxation and he undergone open reduction internal fixation with plate and screws for the lft radius on 22.08.2024 and not the Petitioner complains of pain and weakness in the left wrist, unable to lift weights.

Further deposed that on recent X-ray of the left wrist shows united fracture with implants in situ and the Petitioner has sustained total disability of the left arm at 35%
and whole body disability at 12% and the Petitioner needs another surgery for the removal of implant the estimated of this surgery is Rs.60,000/-.
In support of his oral evidence, the doctor/PW-2 has produced Ex.P-12/Clinical report and Ex.P13 -X-ray.
In the cross-examination of PW-2 by the counsel for Respondent No.2 he has deposed that, he is not treated the doctor of the Petitioner.
He has not seen M.V.C.No.6829/2024 SCCH - 7 the line of treatment of the Petitioner.
The fractures are united and implants inserted was not removed.
There is no difficulties to do his regular business and other activities.
Petitioner is right hand person.
There is no complications to the Petitioner.

Further he has denied that as there is no complications and fractures are united the question of assessing the disability does not arise and he has assessed the disability on his imagination without any basis.
Further he denied that in order to help the petitioner he has assessed disability on the higher side and filed false evidence affidavit and deposing falsely.
25. As the occupation of the petitioner is considered as Hotel business, while doing his work the petitioner has to make wrist movements and he has to put weight on his wrist while doing the work.
But due to injuries sustained in the alleged accident, he is not in a position to do work as earlier.
The doctor stated that the Petitioner has sustained total disability of the left arm at 35% and whole body disability at 12%.
Hence by considering the age, occupation, nature of injury and the functional disability of the petitioner is considered as 12% to the whole body.
With regard to the quantum, age of the petitioner is considered as 29 years and the income is considered at Rs.15,750/- p.m.
As per Sarala Varma's Case the multiplier 17 is applicable and functional disability is considered at 12%.

On considering the avocation and age of the petitioner,
the total loss of future income is calculated as (Rs.15,750/- X 12 X 17 X 12/100) = Rs.3,85,560/-.
Hence, an amount of Rs.3,85,560/- is awarded to the petitioner under the head loss of future income for the disability suffered by him in the accident.

27. In the alleged accident the petitioner has sustained L1 anterior wedge compression fracture,
which shows that definitely the petitioner has suffered pain due to the injuries sustained in the accident, hence an amount of Rs.80,000/- is awarded towards pain and suffering, mental agony.
28.
Further due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient at CDSIMER Hospital for a period from 16.08.2024 to 26.08.2024, i.e., for a period of 11 days.
Therefore this court deems it appropriate to award Rs.33,000/- (Rs.3,000/- per day X 11 days)

30. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the Petitioner would require atleast six months period to recuperate and to get back to his normal day to day activities.
Therefore the Petitioner would be entitled to Rs.94,500/- (Rs.15,750/- x 6 months) under the head loss of income during laid up period.
31. Further the Petitioner has produced hospital and medical bills, towards medical expenses as per Ex.P.9 for an amount of Rs.787/-.

Hence the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.787/-
under the head of hospital and medical expenses.
32. In the evidence affidavit of PW-2/doctor has stated that the Petitioner needs surgery for removal of implants which would cost about Rs.60,000/-.

Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for Rs.60,000/-
compensation under the head future medical expenses.

The details of compensation I propose to award are as under:

The Petitioners are entitled to a total compensation of Rs.7,33,847/-.
35.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fixed on the respondent No.2/Insurance Company and it is directed to deposit the compensation amount.

Thus I conclude that, the Insurance company/Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the compensation amount along with M.V.C.No.6829/2024 SCCH - 7 interest at 6% p.a., from the date of filing of the claim petition.
Hence, I answer issue No.2 is partly in the affirmative.

opennyai_summary.facts:
1. The petitioner filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1989, seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the injures sustained by him in the road traffic accident occurred on 16.08.2024.
2.
Accordingly,
a case was registered in their Crime No.270/2024 and prepared F.I.R. for the offence punishable under sections 281, 125(b) and 106 of BNS and submitted to the jurisdictional judicial Magistrate and the superior M.V.C.No.6829/2024 SCCH - 7 officers and investigation was taken up by the investigating Officer.
Due to the injuries sustained in the alleged accident he lost his income and future prospective life, happiness, and earning capacity and become disabled and dependent.
The alleged accident is occurred due to fault and negligence act of the driver of the offending Car bearing Reg. No.KA-03-AK-4515.
Owner and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the said offending vehicle, as such the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to Petitioner.
Further it has contended that the insured vehicle is not involved in the accident.
The insurer liability is subjected to validity of the DL, permit and other documents as per the law.
opennyai_summary.issue:
:: I S S U E S ::
1. Whether the Petitioner proves that on 16-08-2024 at about 11-30 to 11-35 a.m,
when he was riding the Motor Cycle bearing registration No.KA-05-LM-2259 from Bannerghatta road towards Kaggalipura side along with a pillion rider near Gulakamale Village bridge, Bannerghatta - Kaggalipura Road, Uttarahalli Hobli, Bengaluru South at that time, the driver of offending Car bearing registration No.KA-03-AK- 4515 drove the same in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the said Motor Cycle.
As a result of forced impact, the Petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries?
2. Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?
from whom?
3.
What order or award?
As per final order,
 for the following.......
:REASONS:
opennyai_summary.arguments:
It is contended that the alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The Respondent No.2/Insurance Company admitted that offending vehicle was duly insured with it and its version is that, the alleged accident occurred due to fault of the rider of the unoffending vehicle and no fault of the driver of the offending vehicle and therefore he cannot be held to be negligent.
Further it is alleged that the driver of the offending vehicle is not M.V.C.No.6829/2024 SCCH - 7 possessing valid DL at the time of alleged accident.
As such the insurance company is not liable to pay any compensation and in order to obtained compensation the Petitioner has constrained to file the present claim petition.
Further it is denied that the age, income and occupation of the Petitioner and the petition is false and frivolous in the eye of law and the quantum of compensation claimed by the claimant is exorbitant and sought for dismissal of the petition.
12.
The burden to prove the framed issues lies on the Petitioner.
. The counsel for Respondent No.2 claimed that the said accused to be innocent and further the counsel for Respondent No.2 contended M.V.C.No.6829/2024 SCCH - 7 that, the alleged accident occurred due to fault of the rider/ Petitioner of the unoffending vehicle and no fault of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle, he was driving slowly and therefore he cannot be held to be negligent.
Since the Petitioner has not established M.V.C.No.6829/2024 SCCH - 7 his income, he is not entitled for compensation towards such prospects and hence prays dismissal of the petition.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
On careful reading of Ex.P5/Motor Vehicle Accident Inspection Reports it specifies that the Motor Vehicle Inspector has been clearly opined that, the said accident did not occur because of the mechanical defects in respect of the said offending and unoffending vehicles.
sustained grievous injuries and pillion rider was died due to alleged accident caused by the offending vehicle in question
On going through the prosecution papers, FIR, Spot mahazar, Spot Sketch, Wound Certificate and Charge Sheet and the evidence of PW-1 is specific to the effect that,
the driver of the offending vehicle/accused is the reason for the said incident and at his instance, the incident took place and the alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.
The evidence of Pw.1 is corroborated to the case of the prosecution and he has supported the manner of occurrence in his evidence in the court and the manner of occurrence is the same as alleged in the Ex.P2/complaint.
It is not in dispute as to the aspect that, the Petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the alleged incident.
Because, for the above reasons collectively it is clear that, the accident happened due to rash and negligent act of the accused.
It is evident that injuries noted in the Ex.P6/Wound Certificate would be caused by a road accident.
At the same time, it has come out in evidence that the alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.
Matters being so, acts of the accused person clearly constitute the offences punishable under sections 281, 125(b) and 106 of BNS.
Thus because of such negligent act of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle, it resulted in the injuries of M.V.C.No.6829/2024 SCCH - 7 the innocent young man/Petitioner aforesaid, as he/accused drove the said offending vehicle very rashly or negligently on the spot.
Therefore, the alleged accident occurred due to the fault of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle.
23. It is not in dispute that the Petitioner sustained injuries in the road traffic accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver/accused.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Hence, an amount of Rs.3,85,560/- is awarded to the petitioner under the head loss of future income for the disability suffered by him in the accident.
Therefore this court deems it appropriate to award Rs.33,000/- (Rs.3,000/- per day X 11 days)
30. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the Petitioner would require atleast six months period to recuperate and to get back to his normal day to day activities.
Therefore the Petitioner would be entitled to Rs.94,500/- (Rs.15,750/- x 6 months) under the head loss of income during laid up period.
31. Further the Petitioner has produced hospital and medical bills, towards medical expenses as per Ex.P.9 for an amount of Rs.787/-.
Hence the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.787/-
under the head of hospital and medical expenses.
32. In the evidence affidavit of PW-2/doctor has stated that the Petitioner needs surgery for removal of implants which would cost about Rs.60,000/-.
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for Rs.60,000/-
compensation under the head future medical expenses.
The details of compensation I propose to award are as under:
Sl. Compensation under different heads Amount in No. (Rs) 1 Loss of future income due to disability 3,85,560-00 2 Pain and suffering, mental agony 80,000-00 3
Special diet and conveyance 33,000-00 4 94,500-00 Loss of income during laid up period 5 Loss of amenities 80,000-00 6
Actual medical expenses 787-00 7
Future medical expenses 60,000-00 Total 7,33,847-00 34.
The Petitioners are entitled to a total compensation of Rs.7,33,847/-.
35.
Hence the respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the award amount.
However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fixed on the respondent No.2/Insurance Company and it is directed to deposit the compensation amount.
Thus I conclude that, the Insurance company/Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the compensation amount along with M.V.C.No.6829/2024 SCCH - 7 interest at 6% p.a., from the date of filing of the claim petition.
Hence, I answer issue No.2 is partly in the affirmative.
36. Issue No.3:
In the result I proceed to pass the following: -
ORDER The claim petition filed by the Petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby Partly allowed with cost.
The Petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.7,33,847/- (Rupees Seven lakhs thirty Three thousand Eight Hundred and Forty Seven only) with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
Amount awarded under the future medical expenses does not carry future interest.
Further, Respondent No.2 being insurer of the offending vehicle is directed to deposit the compensation amount together with 6% interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
After deposit, entire compensation amount with interest shall be released in favour of the Petitioner under E-payment with proper verification and identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at  Rs.1,000/-.
Draw the award accordingly.
